Thanks for routing, Vivek. Quick thoughts from Product: 

- High level stance: We can accept a limited "aggregate telemetry / product improvement" clause provided there are clear prohibitions on using raw customer content for model training or creating customer-identifiable outputs. Our priorities are: (a) explicit prohibition on model training on raw customer data unless customer opts in; (b) retention limits for telemetry used in analytics; (c) definitions for "aggregate" and "anonymized" that are measurable.

- Proposed clause (short form): "Provider may collect aggregated, pseudonymized service telemetry and usage metrics derived from Customer interactions for the sole purpose of improving Provider's services, provided that no such data will be used to train generative models on Customer content, and Provider will not retain raw content beyond X days. Aggregated telemetry will be defined as data that cannot reasonably be re-identified to a single Customer or individual, and Provider will maintain documentation of aggregation/pseudonymization processes."

- Retention: propose 90 days for per-session telemetry, 13 months for aggregated summaries (configurable per-account).

- Subprocessors: MetricWorks (analytics) is borderline but acceptable if they have SOC2 Type II + contractual commitments. LogSight (logging) requires a scoped exception: if logs contain customer content, those must be filtered/pseudonymized prior to export. Can we require LogSight to be used only for infrastructure logs (no payload)?

Action items for Security (Mina): can you confirm technical controls and acceptable attestation levels? Also flag anything requiring product change to instrument the required filters/retention.

I am attaching a short revision (rev_analytics_clause_20260904.docx) with redline language. Happy to iterate quickly.

Subject: Re: Fwd: Draft DPA: subprocessors & analytics clause — Security conditions and evidence

Looping in a short security assessment + conditions we need before sign-off. Thanks for the draft clause, Dev — good direction. Conditions: 

1) No raw customer content used for model training or external analytics. Any payload-level data used for analytics must be pseudonymized prior to transfer to a subprocessor.
2) Retention: per-session telemetry retained <= 90 days; aggregated artifacts retention <= 13 months by default.
3) Encryption: all data at rest must be encrypted with customer-segregated keys where feasible; require KMS with HSM-backed keys for WellCare (they asked for this).
4) Subprocessor attestations: require SOC2 Type II + written contractual security commitments (data handling, deletion, breach notification). For any new subprocessor, we require 30 days notice and the ability to object.
4a) LogSight: Acceptable only if used for infrastructure logs (no customer payload). If the integration currently ships payload-level logs, we need a short remediation plan or to switch to an ELT that strips payloads.
5) Audit evidence: we'll provide a security-evidence-pack (attached) with our infra diagrams, encryption proof, and third-party attestations. WellCare may request deeper evidence; we'll require an NDA for full operational logs.

Given the above, Security approves the proposed analytics clause with the listed constraints. Product, please confirm that pseudonymization and retention enforcement are implementable within 2–4 sprints, or advise alternate timeline.

Attachments: security-evidence-pack.zip

— Mina Haddad

Sarah / WellCare Contracts team — thanks for the patience and for routing the DPA. We've reviewed internally across product and security. Summary of what we can commit to and proposed next steps below.

Summary of agreed positions: 
- Analytics: Redwood can accept a narrowly scoped "aggregate telemetry for product improvement" clause. We will explicitly prohibit the use of raw customer content to train generative models or ML weights without customer opt-in. We propose the following short-form language (attached as redline):

  "Provider may collect aggregated and pseudonymized service telemetry derived from Customer interactions for the sole purpose of improving Provider's services and operational reliability. Provider will not use raw customer content to train generative models absent explicit Customer consent. Provider will document its aggregation/pseudonymization process and apply retention limits as set forth below."

- Retention: per-session telemetry <= 90 days; aggregated summaries <= 13 months (default). These are configurable per-account in the Console.

- Subprocessors: Redwood accepts the listed subprocessors provided each maintains SOC2 Type II and signs Redwood's subprocessor addendum. LogSight may only be used for infrastructure logs (no payload). If LogSight is currently receiving payload-level content, Redwood will remediate within 30 days or replace that integration. For any future subprocessor additions, Redwood will provide 30 days notice and allow the customer to object.

- Security controls: data at rest encrypted; KMS/HSM-backed keys for WellCare on request; pseudonymization prior to transfer to external analytics providers; breach notification and attestations as requested. Security has attached an evidence pack.

Next steps / requested items from WellCare: 
1) Please review the attached redline (rev_analytics_clause_20260904.docx) and confirm if the proposed language addresses your analytics requirement.
2) Accept the subprocessors list or flag any showstoppers. If accepted, we'll provide the SOC2 reports and the subprocessor addendum for signature.
3) When you confirm, we'll loop in Legal to finalize the DPA and send a DocuSign packet (link below).
